title: New goal cannot create a goal in any reachable project state: the bootstrap surface offers goal.create at most once per project
description:
FILED BY A FREE AGENT (yaron@cordum.io's standing "let me know when we can use moe-next for real" ask), 2026-08-28 ~00:20 local, from a LIVE drive of the shipped path at a CLEAN materialization of HEAD 55dd65ba (git archive, node_modules junctioned, bundle built with VITE_MOE_LIVE_* unset, daemon started from that tree, demo-seed run, browser paired via playwright). Page dumps + screenshots: C:/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--projexts-moe-next/267e8020-ee4d-4dc9-b5a4-46e4ed922380/scratchpad/lane3/newgoal-shots/ (N1..N5) and newgoal-shots-slow/ (same drive with a 7 s settle before Create, to rule out a first-poll race - same result). Drive script: .../lane3/drive-newgoal.mjs.

WHAT THE OWNER MEETS. task-dc934111 (P1.11b, DONE at 01af2399) enables "New goal". The form opens, Create is disabled until an outcome is typed (good), the operator fills title + outcome + criteria, clicks Create goal - and the form answers, in its refusal slot: "goal.create is not on the affordance surface". No POST /command leaves the page (network log: only /goals/read polls after the pair claim). No goal is created. Same result after 7 s. The form stays open (DoD 3 holds), but the operator has no next step: there is nothing they can do from the browser to make the daemon offer goal.create.

WHY, measured at source and on the wire:
- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts:51-53 `goalCreateOffer` = `frame.offers.find(commandKind === "goal.create")`; :91-93 answers the refusal above when it is null. The offer's commandId/expectedVersion are needed for the dispatch (DoD 4 keeps the submitted data as payload; that part is fine).
- The daemon's POST /affordances/read on the seeded project (curl with the lane operator credential) answers 14 steps and 8 nextAllowedCommands: policy.validate, goal.close, session.open/close/renew x2, node.deliver. goal.create appears ONLY as a step with status COMMITTED @ goal-live-1 and NO offer.
- apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts:193-224 `bootstrapSteps`: for each BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KIND, `if (ledger.kinds.has(kind))` -> COMMITTED and no offer; else if prerequisites missing -> BLOCKED; else -> READY + offer. Keyed on KINDS, not on goals. So the surface offers goal.create exactly once in a project's life: after project.activate commits and before the first goal.create commits.
- Reachable states therefore: (a) seeded / any project with one goal -> goal.create COMMITTED, no offer, New goal always refuses; (b) a fresh `moe init` project -> goal.create BLOCKED behind project.register / bind_repository / provider.probe / project.activate, none of which the browser can drive (the runbook says so: no production writer for that receipt set). The only window in which the button works is between activate and the first goal.create - reachable today solely by hand-driving the chain with curl and stopping before goal.create. That is not a product path.
- Cross-check against lane 1 (same seed, daemon source at 52fda230, 2026-08-27 20:38): its board showed goal.create as READY with a per-read minted target `goal-b8ae16be-...` and goal.create ABSENT from the Committed column (7 committed: approval.decide, plan.propose, policy.install, project.activate, project.bind_repository, project.register, provider.probe). At HEAD the same seed leaves goal.create COMMITTED. `git log -S'goal.create' 52fda230..HEAD -- apps/daemon/src` is EMPTY, so the change is in ledger replay/recognition, not in the surface code - candidates in that range: 55dd65ba (document-identity migration: source-bound identity, legacy replay selection), 9b475aea/04df0ad7 (approve_gate_1 writer), 857d2c89/2f8daa41 (policy risk reader). The architect owns finding which; the row's premise does not depend on it - the once-per-project rule at affordance-read.ts:199 is enough on its own.

WHY A ROW (filing bar): a correctness defect reachable on the shipped path today - the one control the owner was told is now enabled cannot succeed on any project he can reach - and it BLOCKS the owner's named ask (usable for real = PRD in the browser -> goal -> plan -> approve). task-dc934111 is DONE and proved DoD 2 against a stubbed SurfaceFrame that carries a goal.create offer the daemon does not emit; nothing open owns the daemon side. The durable goal catalog already models many goals per project (task-3f71ba30 P2.11 paginates it beyond 256; task-e10e1627 reads distinct briefs), so "one goal per project" is not a product decision the daemon is enforcing - it is the dev bootstrap chain leaking into the product path.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (architect's call): (1) on an ACTIVE project, offer goal.create with a fresh aggregate id on every read regardless of how many goals exist (the minted-per-read target already existed at 52fda230; the control room's work board handles it - work-labels.ts identityPerRead); keep the bootstrap chain's BLOCKED semantics for the pre-activation kinds; OR (2) let the browser create route through the goal-brief command edge (packages/control-room-client buildGoalBriefCommand, task-94b61b0c) against a new aggregate at expectedVersion 0 without needing a surface offer, and have the daemon's ingress validate it as it validates any fresh-aggregate goal.create. Either way the refusal sentence in the form must name a NEXT STEP; "not on the affordance surface" is a diagnosis, not an instruction.

NOT IN SCOPE: the Approve control (P2.15d family), pairing (task-ea0106d7), the stale browser lane at prd-to-approval.spec.ts:88 (noted on task-40017f79).
definitionOfDone: On a project that already holds one durable goal, POST /affordances/read offers goal.create (or the control room's create path no longer depends on that offer), proven by a daemon test that seeds one goal and reads the surface; drilled by restoring the kinds-only branch and observing the arm red.

The live drive (clean materialization, seeded project, browser paired) creates a SECOND goal from the New goal form: POST /command leaves the page, the daemon commits goal.create with the operator's title and outcome, and the goal appears in the goals list from the durable catalog within one poll - quoted from a fresh page dump, not argued.

A fresh `moe init` project either offers goal.create once activated from the browser, or the form's refusal names the exact missing prerequisite and the next step in plain words; no state leaves the operator with a diagnosis and no instruction.
The pre-activation bootstrap kinds keep their BLOCKED semantics and existing prerequisite arms stay green.
taskRails: The control room fabricates nothing: it may only dispatch a goal.create the daemon offers or a command edge the daemon validates; no client-side predicted goal id may enter the list before the catalog returns it (task-dc934111 drill D2b guards this - keep it green).
